questions.question: As per Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2020, what was the difference between death rates of rural and urban India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin 2020 revealed that the death rate in rural India was higher compared to urban India.
 
• The rural death rate was recorded at 6.9 per 1,000 population, while the urban death rate was 5.6 per 1,000 population.
 
• The difference between the death rates of rural and urban areas stood at 1.3 as per the SRS Bulletin 2020.
 
• Death rates are influenced by factors such as healthcare access, lifestyle, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• This data highlights disparities in health infrastructure and living conditions between rural and urban regions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sample Registration System (SRS):**

 
 
• SRS is a demographic survey conducted in India to provide reliable annual estimates of birth rate, death rate, and other vital statistics.
 
• It functions under the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Death Rates:**
 
 
• Access to healthcare facilities, nutrition, sanitation, and socio-economic conditions play a crucial role in determining death rates.
 
• Rural areas often face challenges such as poor healthcare infrastructure and limited access to emergency services.
 
 
 
• **Urban vs. Rural Health Disparities:**
 
 
• Urban areas typically have better access to healthcare facilities, emergency services, and sanitation.
 
• Rural regions may lack adequate medical facilities, leading to higher mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Policy Interventions:**
 
 
• Government schemes like Ayushman Bharat aim to bridge the gap in healthcare access between rural and urban areas.
 
• Improving rural health infrastructure is a key focus area for reducing disparities in death rates.

questions.question: The eponymous track 'Breathless' is one of the most notable works of which music artist, which was released in 1998?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shankar Mahadevan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Breathless'** is one of Shankar Mahadevan's most iconic tracks, released in **1998**, and it gained widespread recognition for its unique style.
 
• The song is composed in a way that it seems like it is sung in one continuous breath, showcasing Shankar Mahadevan's incredible vocal prowess.
 
• Shankar Mahadevan is a renowned Indian singer and composer, part of the celebrated music trio **Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy**.
 
• 'Breathless' was not only a musical masterpiece but also a breakthrough track that catapulted Shankar Mahadevan to fame in the Indian music industry.
 
• The album was produced by **Javed Akhtar**, who penned the lyrics, adding depth to the innovative composition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Shankar Mahadevan is also known for his contributions to Indian classical music and has performed in numerous prestigious concerts worldwide.
 
• He founded the **Shankar Mahadevan Academy**, an online music school aimed at teaching Indian classical music to learners globally.
 
• The music trio **Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy**, of which Shankar Mahadevan is a part, has composed music for several blockbuster films such as **Kal Ho Naa Ho**, **Rock On**, and **Dil Chahta Hai**.

questions.question: What was the motto of the 37th National games held in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Get Set Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 37th National Games of India were held in Goa in 2023, marking an important milestone in India’s sporting history.
 
• The official motto for these games was **"Get Set Goa,"** highlighting Goa's spirit and enthusiasm for hosting a national-level sporting event.
 
• The games featured participation from athletes across the country, competing in multiple disciplines.
 
• Goa was selected as the host state due to its infrastructure and commitment to promoting sports and culture.
 
• The event aimed to foster unity and sportsmanship among players and spectators alike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Games of India:**

 
 
• The National Games are a multi-sport event conducted in India, showcasing talent from across states and union territories.
 
• It is organized under the aegis of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).
 
 
 
• **History:**
 
 
• The first edition of the National Games was held in 1924 in Lahore, then part of undivided India.
 
• It was initially known as the Indian Olympic Games.
 
 
 
• **Frequency:**
 
 
• The games are usually held every two to four years, although delays are common due to logistical and administrative challenges.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The National Games serve as a platform to identify and nurture sporting talent for international competitions, including the Olympics.
 
• They promote physical fitness, national integration, and the spirit of sportsmanship.

questions.question: Pralhad Joshi, who inaugurated the India Sugar & Bio Energy Conference held on 26th and 27th September 2024, is currently heading which Union ministry as of October 2024?

options.text: Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution & New and Renewable Energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution & New and Renewable Energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pralhad Joshi is currently serving as the Union Minister for **Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution & New and Renewable Energy** as of October 2024.
 
• He inaugurated the **India Sugar & Bio Energy Conference** held on 26th and 27th September 2024, showcasing the importance of renewable energy and bioenergy in India's sustainable development goals.
 
• The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution is responsible for **ensuring food security and consumer rights** across India.
 
• This ministry also oversees the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**, which provides subsidized food and essentials to economically weaker sections.
 
• The inclusion of New and Renewable Energy under his portfolio highlights India’s commitment to achieving its **renewable energy targets and transitioning towards sustainable energy sources.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India Sugar & Bio Energy Conference:**

 
 
• A platform to discuss advancements in **sugarcane production, ethanol blending, and bioenergy development.**
 
• Focuses on reducing carbon emissions through the use of biofuels and renewable energy sources.
 
 
 
• **New and Renewable Energy Initiatives:**
 
 
• India aims to achieve **500 GW of renewable energy capacity** by 2030 under its Paris Agreement commitments.
 
• Key projects include the **National Solar Mission** and promotion of wind, hydro, and bioenergy technologies.
 
 
 
• **Public Distribution System (PDS):**
 
 
• An Indian food security system established to distribute essential commodities like rice, wheat, and kerosene to low-income families at subsidized rates.
 
• PDS is critical for alleviating hunger and poverty, especially in rural and economically disadvantaged areas.
 
 
 
• **Ethanol Blending Program:**
 
 
• India has set a target of achieving **20% ethanol blending in petrol by 2025** to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and lower greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Sugar mills play a major role in producing ethanol from molasses, contributing to the program's success.

questions.question: The Indian Association, founded in 1876, was established by:

options.text: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pa
Lala Lajpat Rai and Chittaranjan Das

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Indian Association** was founded in 1876 by **Surendranath Banerjee** and **Anandamohan Bose** in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• The Indian Association was established with the primary objective of creating a strong public opinion against British policies and promoting political unity among Indians.
 
• It aimed to build a platform for educated Indians to demand reforms in British governance and represent Indian issues to the colonial rulers.
 
• The Indian Association played a vital role in organizing the first-ever **Indian National Conference in 1883**, which served as a precursor to the Indian National Congress.
 
• It was one of the earliest organizations that worked towards creating political awareness and fostering unity among Indians during the pre-Congress era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surendranath Banerjee:**

 
 
• He was one of the earliest leaders of India's nationalist movement and is often referred to as the "father of Indian nationalism."
 
• He founded the newspaper **“The Bengalee”** to spread awareness and mobilize public opinion against colonial policies.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee was a key figure in the Indian National Congress and advocated for constitutional reforms and self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Anandamohan Bose:**
 
 
• He was a prominent social reformer, nationalist, and one of the founding members of the Indian Association.
 
• Anandamohan Bose was the first Indian to graduate from the University of Cambridge with honors in mathematics.
 
• He worked actively for the upliftment of society and contributed significantly to the Indian nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Conference:**
 
 
• The Indian National Conference was organized in 1883 and 1885 by the Indian Association to discuss political and social reforms.
 
• It was a precursor to the Indian National Congress and inspired the formation of the Congress in 1885.
 
 
 
• **Pre-Congress Political Organizations:**
 
 
• Before the Indian National Congress, political organizations like the Indian Association, Bombay Presidency Association, and Poona Sarvajanik Sabha laid the foundation of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• These organizations focused on creating political awareness and mobilizing educated Indians for reforms and self-governance.

questions.question: Which dynasty succeeded the Mauryan Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shunga Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shunga Dynasty was established by **Pushyamitra Shunga**, who overthrew the Mauryan emperor Brihadratha in 185 BCE.
 
• Pushyamitra Shunga was originally a **commander-in-chief** in the Mauryan army.
 
• The Shunga Dynasty ruled over parts of northern and central India, with its capital at **Pataliputra**.
 
• The reign of the Shunga Dynasty is marked by the revival of **Brahmanical traditions** and the decline of Buddhism.
 
• The Shunga rulers were patrons of art and architecture, contributing significantly to the construction of **stupas and temples**, including enhancements to the Bharhut and Sanchi stupas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Shunga Dynasty and ruled from 185 BCE to 149 BCE.
 
• He is known for conducting **Vedic sacrifices** such as the Ashvamedha Yajna (horse sacrifice).
 
 
 
• **Decline of Buddhism:**
 
 
• The Shunga period saw a decline in royal patronage for Buddhism, although common people continued to practice it.
 
• The dynasty supported **Brahmanical Hinduism**, leading to a cultural shift.
 
 
 
• **Art and Architecture:**
 
 
• The Shunga rulers are known for their contributions to Indian art, particularly in the form of stupas like Bharhut and Sanchi.
 
• The period also witnessed the development of early Hindu temple architecture.
 
 
 
• **Kanva Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Kanva Dynasty succeeded the Shunga Dynasty after its decline around 73 BCE.
 
• The Kanva rulers were Brahmanical and continued the cultural legacy initiated by the Shungas.

questions.question: The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India is inspired by which country's constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soviet Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were incorporated into the Indian Constitution via the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976.
 
• This concept was inspired by the Constitution of the former **Soviet Union**, which emphasized the duties of citizens alongside their rights.
 
• Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were included; an additional duty was added later through the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution and serve as moral obligations for citizens.
 
• The aim is to promote a sense of responsibility and national unity among Indian citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act (1976):**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution," it introduced several significant changes, including Fundamental Duties, the Preamble, and changes to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A:**
 
 
• It lists 11 Fundamental Duties, such as respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and protecting the environment.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act (2002):**
 
 
• This amendment added the duty of providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 to 14 years.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• While many constitutions focus predominantly on rights, the Soviet Union emphasized both rights and duties to ensure collective responsibility.
 
• India adopted a similar approach to align with its socio-cultural ethos and promote civic responsibility.

questions.question: What is one significant drawback of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loss of biodiversity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution, which began in the mid-20th century, significantly increased agricultural productivity but led to the **loss of biodiversity** as it focused on monoculture farming.
 
• High-yielding varieties (HYVs) of crops like wheat and rice were heavily promoted, replacing traditional crop varieties and reducing **genetic diversity**.
 
• The extensive use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides further degraded ecosystems, harming **pollinators, insects, and soil microorganisms**.
 
• The reliance on a few crop species made agricultural systems more vulnerable to **diseases, pests, and climate change**, as genetic diversity acts as a natural buffer.
 
• Regions with rich agricultural traditions saw the **disappearance of indigenous crop varieties**, which were often better suited to local conditions and required fewer inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monoculture:** The practice of growing a single crop over a large area, which increases productivity but reduces biodiversity and makes crops more susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs):** These are genetically improved crop varieties that produce more output per hectare but require significant inputs like water, fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• **Agrochemical Dependency:** The Green Revolution led to the intensive use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, which caused soil degradation and water contamination.
 
• **Soil Health and Fertility:** Continuous monoculture and excessive chemical use diminished soil organic matter, leading to decreased fertility over time.
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture:** Practices like crop rotation, organic farming, and the use of traditional seeds are being promoted to counteract the negative impacts of the Green Revolution and restore biodiversity.

questions.question: In a state, the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Legislative Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Council of Ministers in a state is **collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly** as per Article 164 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This collective responsibility implies that the entire council works as a unit and stands or falls together in the assembly.
 
• If the State Legislative Assembly passes a vote of no-confidence against the council, all its members including the Chief Minister must resign.
 
• The Chief Minister serves as the leader of the Council of Ministers and communicates the collective decisions of the council to the Governor.
 
• The principle of collective responsibility ensures accountability of the executive (Council of Ministers) to the legislative body (State Assembly).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role**: The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and appoints the Chief Minister and other ministers on the CM’s advice. However, the council is not collectively responsible to the Governor.
 
• **Article 164**: This article lays down the provision of the council's collective responsibility to the legislative assembly and provides the constitutional framework for the functioning of the state government.
 
• **Vote of No-Confidence**: It is a parliamentary motion moved in the legislative assembly to demonstrate that the council no longer has the majority support of the house.
 
• **Individual vs. Collective Responsibility**: While individual ministers are responsible for their respective portfolios, collective responsibility ensures that the council acts unanimously and stands together on all decisions.
 
• **Constitutional Comparison**: This principle of collective responsibility is similar to the responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha at the central level.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement of the following.

options.text: Vitamin C facilitates absorption and utilisation of iron in the body.
Vitamin C plays an important role in collagen synthesis.
Vitamin A, E and C act as antioxidants.
Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fat is considered as a good source of energy during the exercise and competition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fat is not considered a primary source of energy during exercise and competition; carbohydrates are preferred due to their quicker energy release.
 
• During high-intensity exercise, the body primarily relies on glycogen stored in muscles and liver for energy.
 
• Fat metabolism requires more oxygen and takes longer, making it less efficient as a source of immediate energy during exercise.
 
• Fat is utilized as a significant energy source during prolonged, low-intensity activities when carbohydrate reserves are depleted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of Vitamin C:** Vitamin C enhances iron absorption by reducing ferric iron (Fe3+) to ferrous iron (Fe2+), which is more readily absorbed in the intestines.
 
• **Collagen Synthesis:** Vitamin C is essential in the hydroxylation of proline and lysine, which are critical steps in collagen formation.
 
• **Antioxidant Properties:** Vitamins A, E, and C act as antioxidants, neutralizing free radicals and protecting cells from oxidative damage.
 
• **Energy Sources During Exercise:** Carbohydrates are the main energy source for high-intensity exercise, while fats are utilized during prolonged, moderate-intensity activities.
 
• **Metabolic Differences:** Carbohydrate metabolism is anaerobic and faster, while fat metabolism is aerobic and slower but provides sustained energy for long-duration activities.

questions.question: In March 2024, Gyanesh Kumar, a 1988-batch Kerala cadre officer of the Indian Administrative Service, joined which of the following departments of the Indian Government?

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Election Commission of India (ECI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gyanesh Kumar, a 1988-batch Kerala cadre officer of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), was appointed as the **Election Commissioner of India** in March 2024.
 
• The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering elections in India.
 
• The ECI ensures free, fair, and impartial elections for the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, state legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice President.
 
• The Election Commission of India was established on **25th January 1950**, and this date is celebrated annually as **National Voters' Day**.
 
• The appointment of Election Commissioners is made by the **President of India**, and they serve until the age of 65 years or for a tenure of six years, whichever is earlier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI):**

 
 
• The ECI is a three-member body, comprising the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two other Election Commissioners.
 
• The decisions of the ECI are made by a majority vote among the three members.
 
• The ECI has the responsibility to ensure the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) is followed during elections.
 
• Under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the ECI has the authority to supervise, direct, and control the entire election process.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**
 
 
• Article 324: Provides for the establishment of the Election Commission.
 
• Article 325: Prohibits discrimination in the preparation of electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex.
 
• Article 326: Grants universal adult suffrage, allowing all citizens of 18 years and above to vote.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC):**
 
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner is the head of the ECI.
 
• The CEC is appointed by the President of India and can be removed only through impeachment by Parliament, similar to the removal process of a Supreme Court judge.
 
 
 
• **Recent Election Reforms:**
 
 
• Introduction of Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) with Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for greater transparency.
 
• Use of digital technology, including the **cVIGIL app**, to report violations of the MCC.
 
• Facilitation of remote voting for migrant workers, proposed through blockchain technology.

questions.question:
Match the following items.

 
 

 Name of the Scheme
 Year
 
 

 i. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana
 1. 1988
 
 

 ii. The Employee Assurance Scheme
 2. 1989
 
 

 iii. The Million Wells Scheme
 3. 1995
 
 

 iv. National Social Assistance Programme
 4. 1993
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i-2, ii-4, iii-1, iv-3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989):**

 
 
• Launched in **1989** by merging earlier rural employment programs like NREP (National Rural Employment Programme) and RLEGP (Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme).
 
• Objective: To provide employment to the unemployed in rural areas and create durable community assets.
 
• Implemented as a centrally sponsored scheme with a 80:20 cost-sharing ratio between the Centre and the states.
 
 
 
• **The Employee Assurance Scheme (1993):**
 
 
• Launched in **1993** as part of the social security initiatives for employees.
 
• Objective: To provide financial assurance to employees and their families in case of untimely death or disability.
 
• This scheme primarily benefited employees working in the organized sector.
 
 
 
• **The Million Wells Scheme (1988):**
 
 
• Launched in **1988** as a sub-scheme of the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP).
 
• Objective: To provide irrigation facilities and ensure water availability to small and marginal farmers, particularly those living below the poverty line.
 
• It emphasized developing sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme (1995):**
 
 
• Launched in **1995** as part of a broader social welfare initiative by the Government of India.
 
• Objective: To provide financial support to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities belonging to below-poverty-line families.
 
• The scheme includes components like the National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS) and the National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana:**

 
 
• The scheme was later revamped into other rural employment programs like the Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) and subsequently the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS).
 
• It primarily targeted rural poverty alleviation by providing wage employment opportunities to below-poverty-line families.
 
 
 
• **The Million Wells Scheme:**
 
 
• This scheme focused on small and marginal farmers, enabling them to improve their agricultural productivity through better irrigation facilities.
 
• It was particularly beneficial in areas with water scarcity and drought-prone regions.
 
 
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme:**
 
 
• It was one of the first centrally sponsored schemes aimed at providing a safety net to vulnerable sections of society.
 
• Components like widow pensions and family benefits have been crucial in reducing the financial burden on marginalized families.
 
 
 
• **Employee Assurance Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme complemented other social security measures like the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) and the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI).
 
• It emphasized creating a financial safety net for employees working in the formal sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jawahar Rozgar Yojana** is considered a precursor to the modern MGNREGS, which guarantees 100 days of wage employment to rural households.
 
• **The Million Wells Scheme** is notable for its focus on sustainable agriculture and groundwater management.
 
• **National Social Assistance Programme** has evolved to include various direct benefit transfer mechanisms to ensure financial aid reaches beneficiaries directly.
 
• **Employee Assurance Scheme** paved the way for more comprehensive insurance schemes for employees in the organized sector.

questions.question: For Republic Day 2023, which state’s tableau based on the theme 'Manaskhand' was given the best tableau award among the 17 states/union territories tableaux?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uttarakhand's tableau was based on the theme '**Manaskhand**', highlighting the cultural and spiritual heritage of the state.
 
• The tableau showcased the **mythological and historical significance** of the Manaskhand region, which is mentioned in ancient texts like the Skand Purana.
 
• It featured significant religious sites such as **Jageshwar Dham**, known for its ancient temples and rich architectural history.
 
• The tableau emphasized Uttarakhand's unique identity as the '**Devbhoomi**' (Land of Gods) and its natural beauty, including the depiction of the state’s flora and fauna.
 
• Among the 17 states/union territories' tableaux presented during the Republic Day Parade 2023, Uttarakhand's entry was adjudged the best for its artistic, thematic, and cultural excellence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tableaux in Republic Day Parade:**

 
 
• Tableaux are visual representations of cultural, historical, and social themes from different states and union territories.
 
• The Ministry of Defence organizes the tableau competition annually during the Republic Day celebrations.
 
• The tableaux are judged by an expert panel on criteria such as creativity, theme relevance, design, and presentation.
 
 
 
• **Manaskhand:**
 
 
• Manaskhand is a sacred region mentioned in ancient Hindu scriptures, particularly the Skand Purana.
 
• It refers to the area covering parts of modern-day Uttarakhand, known for its temples and spiritual heritage.
 
 
 
• **Jageshwar Dham:**
 
 
• Jageshwar Dham is an ancient temple complex located in Almora, Uttarakhand, dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• The site is considered one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and is a major pilgrimage destination.
 
 
 
• **Devbhoomi (Land of Gods):**
 
 
• Uttarakhand is often referred to as 'Devbhoomi' due to its numerous temples, shrines, and pilgrim sites like Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri.
 
• It is also the origin of sacred rivers like the Ganga and Yamuna.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day Parade 2023:**
 
 
• The 74th Republic Day Parade celebrated India's cultural diversity and military strength at Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath).
 
• A total of 23 tableaux, including those from 17 states/UTs and 6 from various ministries and departments, were part of the parade.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a progressive tax system?

options.text: Tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases
Uniform tax rate for all income groups
Tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases
Higher tax rate for corporations than individuals

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax rate increases as the taxable amount increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A progressive tax system is one where the tax rate increases as the taxable income or amount increases.
 
• This system is designed to impose a higher tax burden on individuals or entities with higher incomes, ensuring equitable distribution of wealth.
 
• It is commonly used in many countries to reduce income inequality and provide funds for public services.
 
• Examples of progressive taxes include income tax brackets, where higher income levels are taxed at higher rates.
 
• The principle of "ability to pay" is central to progressive taxation, meaning those with greater financial resources contribute more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regressive Tax:** A tax system where the tax rate decreases as the taxable amount increases, disproportionately affecting lower-income earners.
 
• **Proportional Tax:** Also known as a flat tax, it applies the same tax rate to all income levels, regardless of the amount earned.
 
• **Examples of Progressive Tax:** U.S. Federal Income Tax, where tax brackets increase with higher income levels.
 
• **Tax Brackets:** Income ranges defined by law where specific tax rates apply, forming the foundation of progressive taxation.
 
• **Redistribution of Wealth:** Progressive taxation aims to reduce economic disparities by transferring resources from higher-income earners to fund programs for the broader population.

questions.question: From which region is the westerly jet stream responsible for bringing western disturbances into the Indian subcontinent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mediterranean**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The westerly jet stream originates from the **Mediterranean region** and is responsible for carrying moisture-laden western disturbances into the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Western disturbances are extratropical storms that bring **rainfall, snowfall, and cloudy weather** to northern India, particularly during the winter months.
 
• These disturbances are crucial for **Rabi crop irrigation**, especially wheat, as they contribute to precipitation in the region.
 
• The interaction of the jet stream with the Himalayan mountains influences the movement and intensity of these disturbances.
 
• The phenomenon is most prevalent in regions such as Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western disturbances:** These are atmospheric depressions originating over the Mediterranean Sea and are carried eastward by the westerly jet stream.
 
• **Jet streams:** High-altitude, fast-flowing air currents in the atmosphere that influence weather patterns globally.
 
• **Impact on agriculture:** Western disturbances are critical for winter precipitation, aiding crops such as wheat and barley in northern India.
 
• **Role of the Himalayas:** The Himalayan range acts as a barrier, forcing these disturbances to deposit their moisture in the northern plains of India.
 
• **Climate significance:** These disturbances play a key role in maintaining seasonal weather patterns and replenishing water resources in India during the winter months.

questions.question: Oli Jerang, a Sattriya dancer, belongs to which of the following states?

• Her performances often highlight the interconnectedness of art and cultural heritage across the northeastern states of India.

• The dance form was primarily performed in **Vaishnavite monasteries** (Satras) as a medium of storytelling.

questions.question: When was the last time India hosted Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1982**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India hosted the **Asian Games in 1982**, marking the 9th edition of the games.
 
• The 1982 Asian Games were held in **New Delhi**, India.
 
• India had previously hosted the inaugural Asian Games in **1951**, making 1982 the second time the country hosted the event.
 
• The mascot for the 1982 Asian Games was **Appu**, an elephant, which became highly popular and symbolic of the games.
 
• The 1982 Asian Games featured a record **4,595 athletes** from 33 nations participating in 21 sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Games:** Also known as the Asiad, it is a continental multi-sport event held every four years, organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).
 
• **Inaugural Edition:** The first Asian Games were held in **1951** in New Delhi, India, marking the beginning of this prestigious event.
 
• **1982 Games Infrastructure:** Notable venues included the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, and Talkatora Indoor Stadium, which were specially constructed or renovated for the event.
 
• **India's Performance in 1982:** India finished 5th in the medal tally with a total of **57 medals** (13 Gold, 19 Silver, and 25 Bronze).
 
• **Legacy:** The 1982 Asian Games played a significant role in upgrading sports infrastructure in India and boosting the popularity of sports across the nation.

questions.question: Who launched the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **8th April 2015**.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **financial support to micro and small enterprises** by offering collateral-free loans through banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), and microfinance institutions (MFIs).
 
• It was introduced to enhance entrepreneurship and promote self-employment, particularly for individuals from weaker sections of society.
 
• The loans under this scheme are categorized into three types: **Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh)**.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) Bank**, which was established as a subsidiary of SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA):**

 
 
• MUDRA Bank was established in 2015 as a financial institution to support the growth of the microfinance sector.
 
• It provides funding to microfinance institutions and NBFCs that, in turn, lend to micro and small enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Collateral-Free Loans:**
 
 
• The Mudra Yojana offers collateral-free loans, which means borrowers do not have to pledge any security or asset to avail the loan.
 
• This reduces the financial burden on small entrepreneurs and encourages more individuals to take up self-employment ventures.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Scheme:**
 
 
• Since its inception, the scheme has significantly contributed to employment generation, especially among women and marginalized sections of society.
 
• A large proportion of beneficiaries under PMMY are women entrepreneurs, highlighting the scheme's focus on gender empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• Individuals, small businesses, and micro-enterprises engaged in manufacturing, trading, and service activities are eligible.
 
• The loans are provided to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.

questions.question: Which of the following can be separated from a mixture by the process of centrifugation, but NOT by the process of filtration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colloid only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **colloid** is a heterogeneous mixture where fine particles are dispersed in a medium but do not settle down due to their small size.
 
• Filtration cannot separate colloidal particles as their size (1-1000 nm) is smaller than the pores of a filter paper.
 
• **Centrifugation** is an effective method for separating colloidal particles by spinning the mixture at high speed, causing the denser colloidal particles to sediment.
 
• Suspensions, in contrast, can be separated by both filtration and centrifugation due to their larger particle size.
 
• Solutions cannot be separated by either filtration or centrifugation, as the solute particles are dissolved at the molecular level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloid:** A mixture where the dispersed particles do not settle or separate on standing. Examples include milk, fog, and jelly.
 
• **Suspension:** A heterogeneous mixture with larger particles (greater than 1000 nm) that settle over time. Examples include muddy water and sand in water.
 
• **Solution:** A homogeneous mixture where solute particles are completely dissolved and cannot be separated by any physical methods like filtration or centrifugation. Examples include saltwater and sugar dissolved in water.
 
• **Centrifugation:** A process of separating components of a mixture based on their densities by spinning it at high speed. It is commonly used in laboratories and industries.
 
• **Filtration:** A mechanical or physical process to separate solids from liquids or gases using a medium that allows only certain particles to pass through (e.g., filter paper).

questions.question: The Bohag Bihu, also called the _________ Bihu is a festival of merriment and heralds, the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rongali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rongali Bihu**, also known as Bohag Bihu, is the most celebrated festival in Assam, marking the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring.
 
• It typically falls in the month of April and lasts for several days, involving vibrant cultural activities, traditional dance, and music.
 
• The festival is divided into three parts: **Goru Bihu** (dedicated to cattle), **Manuh Bihu** (for people), and **Rongali Bihu** (celebration and merriment).
 
• Rongali Bihu represents joy, unity, and the spirit of Assamese culture, with people wearing traditional attires and preparing festive delicacies like pitha and laru.
 
• It is also an agrarian festival, signifying the beginning of the sowing season and honoring nature's bounty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihu Festival**: There are three types of Bihu celebrated in Assam: Rongali (Bohag), Kati (Kongali), and Magh (Bhogali), each having its own significance.
 
• **Cultural Significance**: Rongali Bihu involves traditional dance forms like **Bihu dance** and songs known as **Bihu geet**, which celebrate love, youth, and fertility.
 
• **Agricultural Importance**: The festival marks the beginning of the agricultural season, with farmers praying for a good harvest and prosperity.
 
• **Traditional Attire**: During the celebrations, Assamese people wear traditional clothes like **Mekhela Chador** for women and **Dhoti and Gamosa** for men.
 
• **Global Recognition**: Rongali Bihu is not just confined to Assam but is celebrated by Assamese communities across the world, showcasing their rich cultural heritage.
